summary: Mandatory disposition can turn noisy reviews into process debt, encourage superficial rationales, and let several correlated models manufacture an appearance of consensus.

points.text: Low-precision reviewers can flood a change with plausible findings; requiring an answer to every item shifts the cost of model errors to authors and maintainers.
A reviewer and fixer that share models, prompts, or context may agree on the same false premise. Multiple seats do not create independent evidence.
Teams may write boilerplate acceptance rationales to clear the gate, producing an audit trail that documents compliance without improving the decision.
Blocking all unresolved findings gives a malicious or malfunctioning reviewer denial-of-service leverage unless severity, reviewer authority, and override paths are bounded.
